title: Synergistic integration of green carbon/graphene titanate nanocomposite for high-performance electrochemical detection of mercury( ii ) ions
content: Mercury ions (Hg2+) are considered among the most toxic and persistent heavy metal pollutants due to their severe environmental and biological hazards. Therefore, developing highly sensitive and selective electrochemical sensors for mercury monitoring in aqueous systems has become critically important. In this work, a novel RMGC–GT nanocomposite was successfully synthesized and employed as an efficient electrode modifier for the electrochemical detection of Hg2+ ions using RMGC–GT/GSE as a sensing platform. The synthesized nanomaterial exhibited excellent electrochemical activity owing to its high surface area, enhanced electrical conductivity, and abundant active sites. Structural and morphological characterization of the prepared nanocomposite was performed using different analytical techniques such as X-ray diffraction (XRD), field-emission scanning electron microscopy (FESEM), thermogravimetric analysis (TGA), and Brunauer–Emmett–Teller (BET) analysis, and the functional groups were identified by Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy, confirming the successful formation of the composite structure. Compared with its precursor materials (RMGC and GT), the RMGC–GT nanocomposite exhibited enhanced performance in the detection of Hg2+ ions. The RMGC–GT nanocomposite showed high sensitivity and selectivity, with a detection limit of 140 nM for mercury ions. Furthermore, the nanocomposite exhibited good selectivity, reproducibility, and stability for Hg2+ detection, indicating its promising applicability in environmental monitoring and wastewater analysis.
